fields.products: Treated poles; timber / roundwood products

fields.location: Nalugazi, Busimbi (pole plant); Netulidde trading centre, Kalwana sub-county (sawmill), Mityana (pole plant); Kassanda (Namwasa sawmill)
fields.products: "Located in Mityana district, the NFC's pole plant, which was opened in January 2010, now supplies treated poles" ... "As one approaches the Namwasa Sawmill from Netulidde trading centre in Kalwana sub-county, Kassanda district ... the logs are processed into structural material or pallet material" (Daily Monitor 2024). NFC website: "the additional biomass that is produced from other products at the pole plant and sawmill is converted into renewable energy products".
fields.raw_material_species: Eucalyptus and pine poles from own plantations (Namwasa, Luwunga, Kirinya) plus out-growers; poles sorted 9 to 14 m; CCA treatment (Monitor 2024). Sawmills cut eucalyptus and pine sawlogs (NFC website).
fields.notes: Capacity (as stated): "New Forest is at 120,000 poles" (Observer, 2021); Namwasa sawdust is sold to Uganda Breweries Limited to fire its boilers (Monitor 2024). NFC is in the ERA 2024 notice but not in the live ERA table. The live table lists Sunbird Forests Company Limited at the same Plot 9 Block 164 Nalugazi address with a newforests.earth email (EAFA0367), so it is likely the same pole plant under another entity; confirm. The wood-fuel product is described for the whole group (Uganda and Tanzania) on the website.

fields.products: Veneer, pivoting toward plywood
fields.log_specs: Small-to-medium veneer logs; consistent quantity and quality; certification under exploration
fields.market_orientation: - Mainly export veneer to India but clients in India don’t always fully complete their payments once products have been delivered. The export tax on veneer has made exports harder but they will still export veneer. They have an agreement with an Indian client who will cover 50% of the export tax - So now they prefer to sell to China Chinese clients always complete their payments and you don’t always need to have a contract in place to do business - 60-65% of veneer is grade A - 15% of veneer is grade B - All grades are exported to India and Cambodia - They also make pine veneer which has high demand locally. This pine is sourced from local growers - Overall, with the export ban on veneer, it has pushed them to look for local customers beyond just export buyers of veneer; Yes, already supplying to the markets
fields.supply_strategy: - Natureza has ambitions to own plantations - Mr. Ding has written a letter to local govt to ask for land of about 5,000 acres. They would want at least 1,000 acres if not all 5,000 acres is available - Mr. Ding is looking for good tree seeds - They currently own 50 acres. Half is for the factory and half is for tree planting
fields.notes: Size: Veneer only | Factory: - 240 acres - size of land where the factory is located - 190 acres have been developed and 50 acres have not been developed - The pieces of land are on either side of a main tarmacked road - They produce 80 cbm per day of veneer - They produce different thickness - Veneer is air dried which takes 1 - 2 days depending on the weather - They employ 100 - 150 people. With expansion this will get to 300 people. Natureza is really the only factory in Kilolo. Only factory in any sector not just wood - Current workers, management staff are all university graduate - The technicians have formal training as well - Natureza has partnerships with Ulanzi Technical school. They have some people from technical training schools who are training at the factory - Workers are paid per bale. Factory only has one shift during the day. Factory runs every day throughout the year - Mr. Ding has 2 sets of machines (4 lines) but only uses one set (2 lines) for one shift during the day because NFC canr supply enough timber. If there was enough wood supply, it would be 4 lines*2 shifts - They could ideally consume 4X the current raw material used daily - They have more than 120 workers, of whom 100 are local - [Can't remember context for this conversation??] To fill 5-8 containers he would need a drier that costs 150K USD. This drier would have capacity of 50 - 80 cbm (??) and it would take 6-10 days to dry | Current priorities: Plywood production - Natureza needs to urgently start producing plywood because of the veneer export duty - The export tax was instituted by the Minister of Finance. Used to be 5% but it is now 30% export duty - This policy change is very unpredictable because the govt had said they would be allowed to export veneer till end of Dec 2026 but never mentioned that they would increase the export duty before completely banning veneer exports - [From Mr. Hou of Dazhong] People used to have to pay TZS 500K per container but now have to pay 5 million per container - Natureza has a very nice future but the export tax is making it difficult to do business - Have bought 5 new acres of land where they will be making plywood - They will still sell veneer even after they start making plywood - They will start production as soon as they have enough funding - 1 - 1.5 million USD is the capital gap right now for this phase. This would be for infrastructure and machinery - Plan to have the entire production line to be automated with kiln drying etc. If this does happen, it would bump up - Want to know high value added and certified plywood for European markets Usage of waste - Bio pellets - They have imported machinery to make bio pellets - Will use offcuts and veneer waste to make pellets which will be used instead of charcoal - Pellets will be sold locally though Mr. Ding is aware that there's big demand in Germany - Pellets could also be used by facilities that make soft drinks like soda - Pellets could also be used by a factory making jeans for popular brands in the US who have now moved to Cambodia and TZ (Mkapa EPZ 12 yrs ago) - Why pellets? He met the DG of TIC and he encouraged Mr. Ding to produce pellets so that it can help with reducing use of charcoal - They produce about 20 tonnes of waste per day - They plan to start producing briquettes and pellets by end of this month - Pellets will use veneer waste while briquettes will use offcuts - The machine has capacity to grind (kusaga) waste from veneer peeling at 8 tonnes per day but the speed and capacity in consuming waste reduces as the process proceeds because the drying bit of the production takes time.
